svg.text: A warp, its lanes and its quads
all 32 run the same instruction at the same time
A quad = 4 neighbouring lanes. Not a piece of hardware,
just how the multiply instruction hands out its results.
2. Who holds each value of one multiply's 16 × 8 result
rows 0–7 shown; rows 8–15 go to the same lanes again
Row 0 is held only by lanes 0–3 (quad 0), 2 values each. So a row's max or sum
needs just those 4 lanes to swap values (shuffles), not the whole warp.
runs on one SM (streaming multiprocessor), next to other blocks.
This GPU has 56 SMs, each with its own registers, shared memory and tensor cores.
